newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Rival Cambodian parties clash in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Rival Cambodian parties clash in northwest.

text.p: Rival soldiers allied with the two main parties in Cambodia's coalition government clashed in a key northwest province, officials said on Wednesday.

The number of casualties was unclear as the royalist FUNCINPEC party and communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP) offered different versions of Tuesday afternoon's armed run-in in Battambang province.

Battambang Police Chief Vorn Chhunly, a FUNCINPEC member, said CPP-allied soldiers were being sent to stop a group of recent Khmer Rouge defectors walking out on their CPP commanders in a northwest district.
Forces allied with FUNCINPEC confronted the soldiers and the ensuing clash killed six CPP-allied soldiers, he said.
CPP General Hul Savoeun, military chief of the region, said some 200 FUNCINPEC troops had fired on a mixed force of royalist and CPP troops assigned to development projects.
"They shelled and shot at the group but nobody died," he said, accusing royalists of trying to create tension in the area.
Relations between the two parties have been particularly strained in the main rice-growing province of Battambang in recent months.
Ties between Battambang Governor Ung Samy of the CPP and his deputy, Serei Kosal of FUNCINPEC, plummeted in November after clashes between the two parties left several people wounded.
Ill feelings have continued to simmer despite the intervention of senior officials from both sides aimed at calming the situation.
Co-Interior Minister Sar Kheng proposed earlier this year that the CPP and FUNCINPEC set up a joint committee to sort out problems in the provinces.

The two parties formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993 and have sparred over the issue of power sharing and vied for the allegiance of thousands of defectors from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement.
The Khmer Rouge, whose brutal 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, has been crippled by mass defections since August.
The group reneged on a 1991 peace pact and had been fighting the coalition since 1993.
